title: Passed Pawns
subtitle: A pawn no enemy pawn can stop must be pushed.
goals: Rooks behind passers — and promotion tricks

steps.say: A PASSED pawn has no enemy pawn in front of it — on its own file or either neighbor. Nothing made of pawn can ever stop it, so every step forward is a step toward a new queen. Nimzowitsch said it best: 'The passed pawn is a criminal that must be kept under lock and key.'

steps.prompt: One of your pawns is passed. Find it — and push it!
hints: Check each pawn: is there any black pawn ahead on its file or the neighboring files?
The d-pawn faces no black pawn on c, d or e — nothing can ever block its path. March!

line.say: Push! Black's pawns can only watch — every rank this pawn gains forces Black's PIECES into babysitting duty.

rejections.say: That pawn faces a lifetime of black pawns ahead. The PASSED pawn — the d-pawn — is the one that turns into a queen. Push your passers!

steps.wrongSay: Find the pawn with no enemy pawns on its file or the files beside it — then advance it.
steps.successSay: Passed pawns must be pushed — they gain value with every single step.

steps.prompt: Now the OTHER side of the story: White's passer is two steps from queening. You're Black — lock it down!
hints: A passer must be stopped by a PIECE planted directly in front of it: the blockade.
The knight is the perfect blockader — and yours can reach the square in front of the pawn.

line.say: The blockade! The knight plugs the square in front of the pawn — it's stopped dead, and a knight loses none of its power standing guard. Nimzowitsch would applaud.

rejections.say: e7! The pawn sprints while your knight grazes on the wrong wing — now only desperate measures stop the queening.
e7+! Backed by the rook, the pawn advances WITH CHECK and your king is chained to the blockade forever. Blockading is knight's work — kings have better things to do.

steps.wrongSay: Plant a piece ON the square directly in front of the passer — the knight is built for this.
steps.successSay: Blockade with knights, not kings or queens: the blockader must be happy standing still.

steps.prompt: Your a-pawn dreams of a8. Give it the ideal escort — where does the rook belong?
hints: Tarrasch's famous rule: rooks belong BEHIND passed pawns — yours or the enemy's.
From behind, the rook's power GROWS with every pawn step. From in front, it shrinks.

line.say: Tarrasch's rule in action! The rook pushes from behind like a hand at the pawn's back — and every advance makes the rook's file LONGER, not shorter.

rejections.say: The pawn sprints ahead of its bodyguard — ...Ra8 parks in front, and now YOUR rook must babysit from the side while the pawn is frozen. Rook behind FIRST, push second.
Rxd8 — you traded your only supporter. The lone a-pawn will be surrounded and eaten. Passers need escorts.

steps.wrongSay: Think Tarrasch: which square lets the rook support the pawn for its WHOLE journey?
steps.successSay: Rook behind the passer: the single most quoted rule in endgame strategy — because it wins.

steps.prompt: Your pawn stands one step from glory — but the c8 rook blockades the queening square. Break through NOW!
hints: The blockader holds c8 — so hit it with something it must answer. Deflection!
Rook to d8! Whatever Black does, your pawn promotes — count the captures.

line.say: Deflection! The blockading rook is attacked and has no good square...
The pawn captures DIAGONALLY onto d8 and promotes with check! The blockade never stood a chance once the deflection landed.

rejections.say: Your own pawn blocks the c-file — the rook lift achieves nothing. The blockader must be deflected from the SIDE: Rd8!

steps.wrongSay: The c8 rook is the only thing between your pawn and a crown. Force it to move — or to capture where your pawn can follow.
steps.successSay: Blockades are broken by force: attack the blockader, deflect it, promote. A full passed-pawn masterclass.
